title: detached-network-install-runbook-tf-interface
content:
Summary:

Working notes for installing and upgrading Redwood Private in detached (air-gapped) networks — using the term "detached network" to emphasize controlled ingress/egress windows and strict artifact pre-staging. This doc covers a propose TF module interface, offline registry ingestion workflows, packaged dependency format, and an upgrade canary plan that minimizes on-site touch. Meant to be a pragmatic runbook for SREs and on-site infra engineers.

Goals / constraints:
- Support full on-prem installs without inbound internet access after initial staging.
- Make upgrade rollouts predictable: fail-fast safety gates, preflight validation, and reversible steps.
- Modules should be Terraform-first: operators can instantiate with minimal scripting.
- Bundles must be verifiable (sha256 + signed manifest) and small enough to move via standard USB or SCP windows.

Key concepts / vocabulary:
- detached-registry: on-prem container registry (OCI or Docker) populated from staging nodes during a maintenance window.
- ingest-station: a temporary machine with controlled network access used to pull from public registries, sign, and export bundles.
- package-blob: compressed tarball containing images, charts, manifests, and metadata.json (see format below).
- preflight: local checks run before any upgrade step (image digests, schema checks, k8s admission smoke tests).

Package blob layout (recommended):
  - package.tar.gz
    - metadata.json   (see spec below)
    - images/         (oci-layout or image tarballs)
    - charts/         (helm charts tgz)
    - manifests/      (kustomize overlays, CRDs)
    - signatures/     (sigstore bundle or detached signatures)

metadata.json (plain JSON, small):
  - name: string (e.g., redwood-private-2025-02-01)
  - version: semver-like string
  - created_by: string (ingest-station host + operator)
  - image_index: list of { name, repository, tag, digest, compressed_size }
  - checksums: { package_sha256 }
  - signed_by: list (identities or key ids)
  - channel: stable|canary|rollback

Signature policy:
- All package blobs must be signed by a known ingestion key using sigstore/cosign or PGP. TF module will require a public key fingerprint variable to validate before install.

Ingest station minimal commands (example):
- On ingest-station with internet access:
  - skopeo copy docker://ghcr.io/redwood/engine:1.2.3 oci:local-engine:1.2.3
  - build image archive: ctr -n k8s.io images export images.tar image1 image2 || docker save -o images.tar image1 image2
  - collect charts: helm pull redwood/console --version 0.9.1 --untar --untardir charts/
  - package: tar -czf package.tar.gz metadata.json images.tar charts/ manifests/; sha256sum package.tar.gz > package.sha256
  - sign: cosign sign-blob --key k8s-ingest.key package.tar.gz; mv cosign.sig signatures/

Terraform module interface (notes for module: private_deploy.detached_install):
- Required variables (inputs):
  - name (string): logical name for the deployment
  - namespace (string): install namespace for control-plane
  - package_blob_path (string): path or s3-like URL to pre-staged blob inside detached network
  - registry_endpoint (string): internal OCI registry endpoint to push images to (e.g., 10.0.0.5:5000)
  - verify_key_fingerprint (string): expected fingerprint for signature verification
  - node_selector_map (map of strings): optional node selection for control pods
  - k8s_version (string): expected k8s minor version for compatibility checks

- Optional variables:
  - allow_unverified_install (bool): default false; prevents accidental installs without signature
  - preflight_timeout_seconds (number): default 900

- Outputs (high-level):
  - install_job_id (string): identifier for the background job that performed install
  - applied_manifest_hash (string): digest for the deployed control plane manifests
  - failed_checks (list): comma-delimited string of failed preflight items (empty if none)

Implementation guidance for the TF module:
- Module should not assume direct internet access; it must orchestrate local extraction of the package_blob_path and call a local helper (shell script or provider) to load images into the specified registry_endpoint and apply manifests.
- Prefer using an external provider plugin (make/provider: redwood/package-ingest) that contains the heavy lifting (image load, chart install). This keeps TF declarative surface small and testable.
- Provide a dry-run mode that performs preflight without mutating state. Dry-run must produce the same output as real run for checksum/hash values.

On-site registry populate flow (detached network):
1) Operator copies package.tar.gz to ingest node(s).
2) Run local validation: checksha=$(sha256sum package.tar.gz | awk '{print $1}') compare to metadata checksums and verify cosign signature with stored pubkey.
3) Extract: tar -xzf package.tar.gz -C /var/tmp/redwood-ingest/; load images: for f in images/*.tar; do ctr -n=k8s.io images import $f; done
4) Push to internal registry (if images imported locally): for img in $(cat image_list.txt); do skopeo copy oci:local-engine:${img} docker://${registry_endpoint}/${img}; done
5) Apply CRDs/manifests via kubectl apply -k manifests/ with --server-side for idempotence

Upgrade canary strategy (detached-friendly):
- Pre-stage both old and new package blobs at the site.
- Canary cohort = a set of namespaces or a fixed node pool tagged by label 'upgrade-cohort=canary'.
- Steps:
  1) Run preflight for new package against a staging namespace (non-traffic).
  2) Run smoke tests (see Test matrix) using k8s jobs that validate inference run and metrics export.
  3) If smoke passes, apply new manifests to canary cohort only.
  4) Monitor for 2x expected traffic window or 30 minutes (whichever longer). Rollback if key SLOs break.
  5) If canary passes, roll the rest via batched cohorts, not node-by-node.

Rollback guidance:
- Keep last-known-good package blob on-site. TF module should expose an explicit rollback action (re-apply previous manifests + restore previous image digests).
- For stateful components (databases), follow DB vendor offline restore docs; do not attempt a blind downgrade without backups.

Validation / test matrix (minimum):
- pod-start latency under expected node size (cpu/mem)
- KV cache behavior consistent (kv-cache fill/persist cycles)
- model inference end-to-end: sample prompt -> expected token prefix present in output
- metrics emission to local prometheus pushgateway and correct label cardinality
- security: all control-plane endpoints present server TLS certs matching pinned CA

Operational notes / gotchas observed in previous pilots:
- Large image tarballs (>10GB) cause timeouts with default scp windows; split into chunks and parallelize with rsync --partial.
- Some on-site registries (old Harbor versions) reject OCI index v2 manifests; include an image conversion step during ingest (skopeo copy --format docker-archive if necessary).
- Make sure TLS certs for internal registry are trusted by local nodes; TF module should optionally provision CA bundle into node trust store (controlled change, require ops approval).

Security and compliance recommendations:
- HSM/KMS integration for signing keys on ingest-station; operator keys should be ephemeral and rotated quarterly.
- Keep an immutable store of package blobs with append-only retention for forensic/audit needs.
- Enforce RBAC for the TF module actions via OIDC groups mapping to 'redwood-installers' role.

Open action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype provider plugin: redwood/package-ingest (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Define metadata.json schema as JSON Schema and add unit tests for parser (owner: Marco)
- [ ] Add cosign verification step to TF module; gate with verify_key_fingerprint (owner: Jon)
- [ ] Pilot with customer X in Europe (ticket JIRA-8590) during maintenance window Q1 2025

Notes for documentation and operator UX:
- Keep the TF call as simple as: module "site_install" { source = ".../detached_install" package_blob_path = "/data/blobs/redwood-2025-02-01.tar.gz" registry_endpoint = "10.10.0.5:5000" verify_key_fingerprint = "sha256:abcd..." }
- Provide a one-command helper: redwood-offline install --blob /path/to/package.tar.gz --registry 10.10.0.5:5000 which internally calls the provider and streams logs.

References and links:
- Detached playbook draft (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Detached+Network+Playbook
- TF provider prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/tree/offline-ingest
- Pilot notes: JIRA-8590, JIRA-4567

End of runbook draft.
